name: Keith Rabois

summary.text: Keith Rabois graduated from Stanford in 1991 and was part of the Stanford Review circle around Peter Thiel. In 1992, while studying law at Stanford, he directed anti-gay slurs at a campus residence, The Stanford Daily reports, and in a letter to the Daily he defended the remarks as provocative free speech. Amid the controversy he left Stanford's law program and continued his studies at Harvard. He says he clerked on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit and practiced for about three and a half years at the Wall Street law firm where Thiel had briefly worked, then joined voter.com in February 2000. He says Thiel recruited him to PayPal; TechCrunch dates his PayPal tenure from late 2000 to late 2002. PayPal's 2001-2002 IPO filings do not list him among executive officers or key employees. No record found of other pre-1999 finance, government or intelligence roles.

facts.claim: After PayPal, Rabois was an early executive at LinkedIn and at Slide (later acquired by Google), then joined Square in August 2010, where as chief operating officer he ran most non-product functions, including marketing, communications, business development, distribution, human resources and risk management. He also sat on the boards of Yelp and Xoom.

sources.title: Keith Rabois Leaves Top Operating Role At Square

facts.claim: Rabois resigned as Square's COO in January 2013. Square said it first heard of the allegations when it received the threat of a lawsuit two weeks earlier. It said it ran a full investigation and did not find evidence to support any claims, but that he 'exercised poor judgment that ultimately undermined his ability to remain an effective leader at Square.' Rabois said the relationship 'was welcome' and that continuing a physical relationship after the man began working at Square was poor judgment. He said Square did not know of the relationship before the suit was threatened, and he denied the other accusations. He said the threatened suit 'feels like a shakedown.'

sources.title: Rabois Left Square Over Sexual Harassment Claim, Calls Accusations "A Shakedown"

facts.claim: Fortune reported that, according to Square and Rabois, the former employee had threatened a sexual harassment suit unless paid millions of dollars, and that no lawsuit had been filed as of late February 2013. Vinod Khosla is a Square board member with full access to the investigation's results. Fortune reported that he was comfortable with Square's finding that Rabois had committed only an error in judgment. The same month Khosla Ventures announced Rabois was joining it as a senior investment professional. Fortune listed his early angel investments as including YouTube, LinkedIn, Airbnb and Eventbrite.

sources.title: Ex-Square executive Keith Rabois joining Khosla Ventures

facts.claim: Opendoor, co-founded by Rabois, Eric Wu, Ian Wong and JD Ross, raised $9.95 million in a round led by Khosla Ventures, where Rabois worked. Individual investors named included PayPal alumni Max Levchin, David Sacks and Jeremy Stoppelman, plus Sam Altman and others. TechCrunch later reported that Rabois came up with the idea for Opendoor at Khosla and provided its seed funding. Opendoor's 2025 release gives 2013 as the founding year.

In November 2020 Rabois said he was moving from San Francisco to Miami. He cited San Francisco's governance ('so massively improperly run and managed'), Florida having no state income tax, and the climate. In February 2021 Founders Fund signed a one-year lease on a 2,073-square-foot Miami office, and the firm said Rabois would be based in Miami full-time.

In January 2024 Rabois left Founders Fund and returned to Khosla Ventures. He said he had left Khosla in 2019 because 'I hated coming down from SF to Sand Hill Road,' that he would stay in Miami, which he called the future of America, and that Khosla planned a Miami office. Opendoor's September 2025 release still identified him as a Managing Director at Khosla Ventures. No public record found of a later return to Founders Fund.
facts.quote: I think the future of America is going to be based in Miami.

sources.title: Opendoor Names Kaz Nejatian as CEO; Founders Rabois and Wu Rejoin Board

facts.claim: On September 10, 2025, Opendoor named Shopify's Kaz Nejatian CEO and said co-founders Rabois and Eric Wu were returning to its board, with Rabois as Chairman. Opendoor said it had entered securities purchase agreements with Khosla Ventures, where Rabois is a Managing Director, and with Wu to invest $40 million of equity through a private investment in the company. The release did not disclose price or share count.

sources.title: Opendoor Names Kaz Nejatian as CEO; Founders Rabois and Wu Rejoin Board

facts.claim: Fortune reported that Opendoor shares had traded below $1 for most of 2024 and 2025 and rose about 80% after the leadership change was announced. As chairman, Rabois said the company's roughly 1,400 employees were far more than needed and that its remote-work culture was broken. The article did not report layoffs actually carried out.
facts.quote: There's 1,400 employees at Opendoor. I don't know what most of them do. We don't need more than 200 of them.

facts.claim: FEC records list Rabois (employer Founders Fund or Khosla Ventures; San Francisco and Miami Beach) giving to House Republican joint fundraising committees. To Take Back the House 2022 he gave $500,000 on 2021-03-26, $271,900 on 2021-09-28 and $597,800 on 2022-02-21. He gave $693,700 to Protect the House 2024 on 2023-03-15, $500,000 to Grow the Majority on 2024-02-16 and $200,000 to Scalise Leadership Fund 2024 on 2024-02-29. He also gave $500,000 to the Congressional Leadership Fund, the House GOP super PAC, on 2024-02-20.

facts.claim: FEC records list Rabois giving to Senate Republican committees: Senate Georgia Battleground Fund ($154,100 on 2020-11-12, before Georgia's runoffs), Rick Scott Victory Fund ($260,000 on 2022-04-25) and NRSC Victory ($400,000 on 2024-05-08).

sources.title: Individual contributions, contributor name Rabois, 2019-2024, $50,000 or more

facts.claim: In a September 2022 interview with Fortune, before any 2024 candidate had announced, Rabois said he would be 'excited' about Ron DeSantis as president. He praised Florida's 'anti-tax and anti-regulation base' and called ESG investing 'a fraud.' In October 2023 ABC News reported that Rabois and his husband would host a $10,000-per-guest reception for DeSantis's rival Nikki Haley. That was about three months after he had told a Fortune conference that they were significant DeSantis supporters. FEC records show him giving $700,000 (2023-09-13) and $300,000 (2024-01-12) to SFA Fund Inc., the hybrid PAC backing Haley.

openQuestions: The brief names Sidley Austin as Rabois's law firm. No source opened in this session supports that. Rabois says he worked at the same Wall Street firm as Thiel, and PayPal's 10-K places Thiel at Sullivan & Cromwell; secondary profiles (not opened) also name Sullivan & Cromwell.
Rabois's exact PayPal title (often given as Executive Vice President, Business Development, Public Affairs and Policy) comes only from his LinkedIn and secondary profiles, which were not opened.
Harvard J.D. year (often given as 1994) and the name of the Fifth Circuit judge he clerked for were not confirmed in an opened source.

Stanford's February 12, 1992 news release on the incident (news.stanford.edu/pr/92/920212Arc2432.html) is behind a bot check and was not read; the full text of Rabois's 1992 letter to The Stanford Daily was not found.
No public record found of Rabois holding finance-industry, government (beyond a federal judicial clerkship) or intelligence roles before 1999, or of outside funding tied to him before PayPal.
Exact LinkedIn (reported Jan 2005-May 2007) and Slide (reported May 2007-Aug 2010) titles and dates come from his LinkedIn profile via Wikipedia; not confirmed in a primary source opened here.
Whether the threatened 2013 lawsuit was ever filed or settled: no public record found in sources opened.
No record found of Rabois holding an interim or returning CEO role at Opendoor; 2025 sources show him as Chairman with Kaz Nejatian as CEO.
Wikipedia cites a NYT live blog saying Rabois hosted JD Vance at a 2024 Trump fundraiser; not opened or verified.
The Real Deal reported a $50,000 gift from Rabois to Miami Mayor Francis Suarez's PAC (2021); page returned 403, not verified.
FWD.us (2013 immigration lobbying group) listed Rabois as a major contributor per an archived page cited by Wikipedia; archive not reachable.
FEC pull covered the top 25 contributions by size only (1,095 records total); smaller and pre-2020 gifts, including any to Democrats, were not reviewed because of API rate limits.
Ties to Musk and Andreessen after 2002 not documented in sources opened here.
